title: Refusals on the hosted card
summary: The hosted card's four refusals drawn the DL6 way: a full license (Replace a device), every license full (Replace a device on the one that ranks first), a license bought with another email (Use another account), and no key entries left (Sign in instead). Each says what happened in a neutral callout and offers the fix as the one primary.
compare: Every refusal is a neutral callout on the sunken surface with a glyph, a strong first line and one sentence; no amber, no danger, no warning pill (B8, auth-08/09/10).
The fix is always the one primary (ink, block); there is never a disabled primary or a dead end: a second, quiet way out where one exists.
Full licenses show a neutral 'Full' pill and their device counts in words; the seat meter, if drawn, is neutral.
Key entries used up names when entries come back and turns the primary into Sign in instead; the key on-ramp header has no request verb (frame 4).
Amber is kept only for 'unsynced changes' on sign-out (not on this board).
Each frame keeps the product header strip; in a landscape window the same bodies sit in the form pane beside the passport.
